title: There Is Life Hiding Inside Earth

blocks.en_text: We’ve found a new planet, home to octillions  of the most extreme beings living in the
blocks.zh_text: 我们发现了一颗新行星，上面住着数以亿亿计的最极端生物，它们生活在

blocks.en_text: most absurd and deadly hellscape. In absolute  darkness, crushed by the weight of mountains,
blocks.zh_text: 最荒诞、最致命的炼狱里。在绝对的黑暗中，被山峦的重量压着，

blocks.en_text: starved of oxygen, cooked alive, bathed  in acid, salt or radiation. And yet,
blocks.zh_text: 缺氧、被活活烤着，泡在酸、盐或辐射里。可即便如此，

blocks.en_text: they live for thousands, perhaps  millions of years! It turns out,
blocks.zh_text: 它们能活上几千年，甚至几百万年！原来，

blocks.en_text: this planet is not in space –––  it is inside the crust of Earth!
blocks.zh_text: 这颗行星不在太空里——它就在地球的地壳内部！

blocks.en_text: This is the deep biosphere and  we basically learned that it
blocks.zh_text: 这就是深层生物圈，而我们基本上昨天才刚知道

blocks.en_text: exists yesterday. Its volume is at least  twice as large as all the Earth’s oceans,
blocks.zh_text: 它的存在。它的体积至少是地球所有海洋的两倍，

blocks.en_text: home to more microbes than the rest of  the entire planet.Their total biomass
blocks.zh_text: 里面的微生物比整个星球其他地方加起来还多。它们的总生物量

blocks.en_text: is more than 20 times greater than all  humans, livestock, and animal wildlife.
blocks.zh_text: 是所有人类、牲畜和野生动物总和的二十多倍。

blocks.en_text: Let’s descend into this mad,
blocks.zh_text: 让我们下潜进入这个疯狂、

blocks.en_text: deadly world where none of the rules we  thought are mandatory for life apply.
blocks.zh_text: 致命的世界，在那里，我们以为生命必需的所有规则都不适用。

blocks.en_text: Going Deeper and Deeper
blocks.zh_text: 越挖越深

blocks.en_text: Deep life seems to be everywhere we  look: below the oceans, near volcanoes,
blocks.zh_text: 深层生命似乎无处不在：海洋之下、火山附近、

blocks.en_text: beneath the glaciers of Antarctica, under any  landscape we can imagine and anywhere we live.
blocks.zh_text: 南极洲的冰川之下，任何我们能想象到的地貌之下，以及我们居住的任何地方。

blocks.en_text: We’ll use a special duck science drill and  start our journey in familiar territory:
blocks.zh_text: 我们要用一台特别的鸭子科学钻机，从熟悉的领域开始我们的旅程：

blocks.en_text: on land, in the soil, where plants grow  and animals roam. If earth were an onion,
blocks.zh_text: 陆地上，土壤里，植物生长、动物漫步的地方。如果地球是一颗洋葱，

blocks.en_text: this is the very top of the very top layer.  Soil is a lavish four-way partnership of air,
blocks.zh_text: 这里就是最顶层的最上面。土壤是空气、

blocks.en_text: water, minerals and organic matter, bathed  in endless energy. Life lives in luxury here.
blocks.zh_text: 水、矿物质和有机物奢华的四方合作，沐浴在无尽的能量中。这里的生命过得养尊处优。

blocks.en_text: Plants exploit this paradise and produce more  than 30 times the biomass of all of Earth’s
blocks.zh_text: 植物利用这片天堂，每年产生的生物量超过地球所有

blocks.en_text: animals each year, in a constant cycle of growth  and decay. Only a tiny fraction of the biomass is
blocks.zh_text: 动物的三十倍，处于不断生长和腐烂的循环中。只有极小一部分生物量

blocks.en_text: buried deeper in the ground, supplying juicy  resources for almost half a billion years.
blocks.zh_text: 被埋进更深的地下，为近五亿年提供丰富的资源。

blocks.en_text: As we dig deeper, most of the  air has been squeezed out and
blocks.zh_text: 随着我们越挖越深，大部分空气都被挤了出去，

blocks.en_text: we cross the water table into a  zone saturated with groundwater,
blocks.zh_text: 我们穿过地下水位，进入一个充满地下水的区域，

blocks.en_text: rich in minerals and some organic matter. Roots  from the most ambitious plants reach down here,
blocks.zh_text: 富含矿物质和一些有机物。最有野心的植物的根会伸到这里，

blocks.en_text: and the most common inhabitants are  scavengers living off decay. This
blocks.zh_text: 而最常见的居民是以腐败物为生的食腐生物。这

blocks.en_text: layer can be pretty cold because it is still  slowly warming up from the most recent ice age.
blocks.zh_text: 一层可能相当冷，因为它还在从最近的冰期缓慢升温。

blocks.en_text: Klunk
blocks.zh_text: 克朗克

blocks.en_text: We reach bedrock. A foundation of solid rock for  all the less solid stuff above, home to fractures
blocks.zh_text: 我们到达了基岩。它是上方所有不那么坚固的东西的坚实岩石基础，也是裂缝的家园

blocks.en_text: filled with water . It can be exposed to the  surface, or buried hundreds of meters below stuff.
blocks.zh_text: 裂缝里充满了水。它可能暴露在地表，也可能被埋在下方数百米深的地方。

blocks.en_text: Here, in the dense bedrock, we’re in a weird  planet inside the planet. The most thrilling
blocks.zh_text: 在这里，在致密的基岩中，我们身处一个星球内部的奇异世界。这是最令人兴奋的

blocks.en_text: zone of the deep biosphere. As we drill further  down, temperatures gradually begin to rise,
blocks.zh_text: 深层生物圈区域。随着我们继续向下钻探，温度逐渐开始上升，

blocks.en_text: and soon it gets really hot and the pressure  rises. Underneath 400 meters of rock,
blocks.zh_text: 很快就会变得非常热，压力也随之升高。在400米厚的岩石之下，

blocks.en_text: the pressure is similar to the surface of  Venus. We drill faster now, down to 1000 meters,
blocks.zh_text: 压力与金星表面相似。现在我们钻得更快了，一直下到1000米，

blocks.en_text: deeper than the Burj Khalifa is tall. It is about  30°C , and there is almost no free oxygen left.
blocks.zh_text: 比哈利法塔的高度还深。温度大约是30°C，而且几乎没有游离氧了。

blocks.en_text: We continue and finally stop almost  4 kilometers down. Above us pressing
blocks.zh_text: 我们继续前进，最终在将近4公里深处停下。在我们上方，压着

blocks.en_text: solid rock weighing tens of thousands of  tons with pressures as intense as at the
blocks.zh_text: 重达数万吨的坚硬岩石，压力之强堪比

blocks.en_text: bottom of the Mariana Trench. Down here it is on  average 120 degrees C , even hotter if a magma
blocks.zh_text: 马里亚纳海沟底部。这里平均温度是120摄氏度，如果附近有岩浆

blocks.en_text: plume is nearby. The heat is a leftover from  Earth's formation and from from the decay of
blocks.zh_text: 柱的话还会更热。这些热量是地球形成时留下的余热，也来自

blocks.en_text: radioactive elements like thorium and uranium  that shower the crust with a constant wave of
blocks.zh_text: 钍和铀等放射性元素的衰变，它们向地壳持续释放一波波

blocks.en_text: radioactivity. To make things worse some rocks  are mixed with extreme amounts of salt. Hell.
blocks.zh_text: 放射性。更糟的是，有些岩石混有极大量的盐。简直是地狱。

blocks.en_text: And yet. Life is thriving. Inside rock! If we zoom  in, we see that solid rock is not actually solid!
blocks.zh_text: 然而。生命却在这里繁盛。就在岩石里面！如果我们放大来看，会发现坚固的岩石其实并不坚固！

blocks.en_text: It’s traversed by cracks, voids and tiny pores.  Sandstone, limestone or basalt are so porous that
blocks.zh_text: 它布满了裂缝、空洞和微小的孔隙。砂岩、石灰岩或玄武岩孔隙极多，以至于

blocks.en_text: up to 40 percent of their volume is actually empty  space. But even much denser rocks like granite,
blocks.zh_text: 其体积中多达40%其实是空的。但即便是花岗岩这样致密得多的岩石，

blocks.en_text: can be split open by cracks and fractures.  We’ve found a gigantic planet spanning
blocks.zh_text: 也能被裂缝和断裂劈开。我们发现了一个横跨整个星球的巨大

blocks.en_text: system of micro-caves, free real estate  filled with water and hardcore microbes!
blocks.zh_text: 微型洞穴系统，这是充满水和硬核微生物的免费房地产！

blocks.en_text: And these caves are moving.
blocks.zh_text: 而这些洞穴还在移动。

blocks.en_text: Just like the atmosphere is constantly mixing  air to create weather, down here rocks are
blocks.zh_text: 就像大气层不断混合空气、形成天气一样，这里的岩石也在不断混合，

blocks.en_text: mixing to create rock weather. Submerged  mountain ranges are shifting and ripping,
blocks.zh_text: 形成“岩石天气”。水下的山脉在移动、撕裂、碰撞、合并。

blocks.en_text: crashing and merging. Continents  smash into each other with the
blocks.zh_text: 大陆彼此撞击，能量相当于数百万枚核武器，

blocks.en_text: energy of millions of nuclear weapons  but as slow as your fingernails grow.
blocks.zh_text: 但速度却和你指甲生长的速度一样慢。

blocks.en_text: Countless tiny and not so tiny earthquakes  rip open tiny new fissures and passageways,
blocks.zh_text: 无数大大小小的地震撕开新的细小裂缝和通道，

blocks.en_text: creating new spaces for life and closing others  off forever. In this hot, moving pressure cooker,
blocks.zh_text: 为生命创造新的空间，也把另一些空间永远封死。在这个炽热、不断运动的压力锅里，

blocks.en_text: minerals are forged and baked, and  organic molecules are created and
blocks.zh_text: 矿物被锻造、烘烤，有机分子被创造出来，

blocks.en_text: destroyed. An insane menu for anyone  brave enough to try to survive down
blocks.zh_text: 又被摧毁。对于任何敢于在这里生存的生命来说，这是一份疯狂的菜单。

blocks.en_text: here. Let us venture into the system  of tiny caves and meet some of them.
blocks.zh_text: 让我们走进这个由微小洞穴组成的系统，去认识其中的一些居民。

blocks.en_text: The Most Extreme Living Things
blocks.zh_text: 最极端的生物

blocks.en_text: We think that octillions  of microbes live down here,
blocks.zh_text: 我们认为这里有数以亿亿计的微生物，

blocks.en_text: and naturally they are pretty hardcore.  The doomsday preppers of the underworld.
blocks.zh_text: 它们自然都相当硬核，堪称地下世界的末日准备者。

blocks.en_text: Some have big, bulky genomes, living entirely on  their own, basically forming their own ecosystem.
blocks.zh_text: 有些拥有庞大笨重的基因组，完全靠自己生活，基本上自成一个生态系统。

blocks.en_text: Like the bacterium Desulforudis audaxviator.  It synthesises its own food by nibbling carbon
blocks.zh_text: 比如细菌 Desulforudis audaxviator。它靠啃食岩石中的碳或硫来合成自己的食物，

blocks.en_text: or sulfur from the rock and turning it into  organic substances. If the conditions get
blocks.zh_text: 把它们转化成有机物质。如果环境变得过于极端，或者周围没有食物，

blocks.en_text: too extreme or if there is no food around,  it kills itself to survive, by forming an
blocks.zh_text: 它就会为了生存而杀死自己，方式是形成一个内生孢子。它分裂成一大一小两部分，

blocks.en_text: endospore. It divides into a big and a small part,  and swallows the small part again, forming a cell,
blocks.zh_text: 再把小的那部分吞回去，形成一个细胞中的细胞。

blocks.en_text: within a cell. The outer cell then sheds its  water and kills itself, leaving the spore to
blocks.zh_text: 外层细胞随后脱去水分并自我消亡，留下孢子

blocks.en_text: float around, maybe for thousands of years until  it finds a good place to spring to life again.
blocks.zh_text: 四处漂浮，也许漂浮几千年，直到找到合适的地方重新焕发生机。

blocks.en_text: Others like some company, like the archaea  with the clunky name Altiarchaeum hamiconexum,
blocks.zh_text: 另一些则喜欢结伴，比如名字拗口的古菌 Altiarchaeum hamiconexum，

blocks.en_text: that have a rare double membrane covered in  weird materials that protect them against
blocks.zh_text: 它们有一层罕见的双层膜，上面覆盖着奇怪的物质，保护它们抵御

blocks.en_text: the extremes. They shoot out nano-sized  grappling hooks to tether themselves and
blocks.zh_text: 极端环境。它们射出纳米级的抓钩把自己固定住，

blocks.en_text: seem to live in cracks and fissures filled  with water completely devoid of oxygen,
blocks.zh_text: 似乎生活在充满水、完全没有氧气的裂缝和裂隙中，

blocks.en_text: harvest carbon dioxide to create  biomass, and may sort of eat hydrogen.
blocks.zh_text: 吸收二氧化碳来制造生物质，还可能以某种方式吃氢气。

blocks.en_text: The conditions in the deep biosphere are so  harsh that other microbes share the hard work
blocks.zh_text: 深部生物圈的条件极其恶劣，所以其他微生物会分担这份苦活，

blocks.en_text: by forming consortia. They knit themselves  together in a biofilm – a very thin, sticky
blocks.zh_text: 办法就是结成共生体。它们彼此编织在一起形成生物膜——一张非常薄、黏糊糊的

blocks.en_text: net that shields them against the extremes. They  are miniature cells, often with a small genome,
blocks.zh_text: 网，保护它们抵御极端环境。它们是微小的细胞，通常基因组也很小，

blocks.en_text: but each good at one thing. One type of microbe  eats methane and excretes its electrons. A second
blocks.zh_text: 但各自擅长一件事。一种微生物吃甲烷，排出电子。第二种

blocks.en_text: type eats these electrons and converts sulphate  into sulfite that is then eaten by a third microbe
blocks.zh_text: 吃这些电子，把硫酸盐转化成亚硫酸盐，然后亚硫酸盐又被第三种微生物吃掉，

blocks.en_text: and so on. Some eat iron, others use electrons  to turn nitrogen or carbon dioxide into biomass.
blocks.zh_text: 如此循环。有的吃铁，有的用电子把氮或二氧化碳转化成生物质。

blocks.en_text: Life down here found ways to use stuff that  is poisonous to most animals to make food and
blocks.zh_text: 这里的生命找到了办法，把对大多数动物有毒的东西变成食物和

blocks.en_text: energy. But still, life is incredibly hard and  resources and energy are super hard to come by.
blocks.zh_text: 能量。但即便如此，生存依然极其艰难，资源和能量都极难获得。

blocks.en_text: So the most intense strategy for survival  down here is to live forever. Like monks
blocks.zh_text: 所以在这里，最极致的生存策略就是永远活下去。就像

blocks.en_text: who’ve taken a vow of poverty, deep microbes  consume very little and conserve their energy.
blocks.zh_text: 立下清贫誓言的修士，深部微生物消耗极少，并节省自己的能量。

blocks.en_text: Their metabolism is up to a million times  slower than microbes at the surface. They
blocks.zh_text: 它们的新陈代谢比地表微生物慢上百万倍。它们

blocks.en_text: had a meal when you were born and are still  digesting it. For most of their life they exist
blocks.zh_text: 在你出生时吃了一顿饭，到现在还在消化。它们一生大部分时间都

blocks.en_text: in a slow limbo – some even slowly cannibalise  themselves. Until a sudden influx of resources
blocks.zh_text: 处在缓慢的停滞状态——有些甚至慢慢吞噬自己。直到资源突然

blocks.en_text: arrives by pure chance – and then they spring  into action and reproduce. With this lifestyle
blocks.zh_text: 纯靠运气涌来——它们便立刻行动起来，开始繁殖。靠着这种生活方式，

blocks.en_text: it seems that extreme microbes can live for  centuries, maybe even for millions of years!
blocks.zh_text: 极端微生物似乎能活上几百年，甚至可能活上几百万年！

blocks.en_text: If they are not hunted to death, of course.  Because kilometers deep in limestone habitats,
blocks.zh_text: 当然，前提是它们没被猎杀至死。因为在几千米深的石灰岩栖息地里，

blocks.en_text: there seem to be spaces big enough for  multicellular predators. We found asexual worms,
blocks.zh_text: 似乎有足够大的空间容纳多细胞捕食者。我们发现了无性繁殖的蠕虫，

blocks.en_text: 100 times longer than microbes, hunting  and devouring bacteria. It's not clear
blocks.zh_text: 比微生物长100倍，正在捕猎并吞食细菌。目前还不清楚

blocks.en_text: if they originated down here or if  mini earthquakes opened up fractures
blocks.zh_text: 它们是本来就起源于这里，还是小地震打开了裂缝，

blocks.en_text: for water to carry them into the deep.  But there are other fierce predators
blocks.zh_text: 让水流把它们带到了深处。但还有其他凶猛的捕食者

blocks.en_text: like rotifers or arthropods in the  depths, hunting immortal microbes.
blocks.zh_text: 比如深处的轮虫或节肢动物，正在捕食永生的微生物。

blocks.en_text: We wish we could tell you more insane things  about life in the deep biosphere but there is
blocks.zh_text: 我们很想再多告诉你一些关于深层生物圈生命的疯狂事实，但是

blocks.en_text: a problem. We don’t know that much yet. For one,  we can not really get a good look under kilometers
blocks.zh_text: 有个问题。我们目前知道的还不太多。首先，我们没法真正好好看清几公里厚的岩石下面

blocks.en_text: of rock. Drilling down could contaminate  the samples with microbes from the surface.
blocks.zh_text: 是什么样子。往下钻探可能会让样本被地表的微生物污染。

blocks.en_text: We found living ones in deep mines  and brought them into the lab. But
blocks.zh_text: 我们在深矿井里找到了活着的微生物，并把它们带进了实验室。但是

blocks.en_text: it is pretty hard to simulate the conditions  they feel comfy in – in boiling hot water,
blocks.zh_text: 要模拟出它们觉得舒服的环境相当困难——在滚烫的热水里，

blocks.en_text: squeezed under mountains, submerged in  deadly chemicals – and still see them
blocks.zh_text: 被压在山脉之下，浸泡在致命的化学物质中——而且还要能透过显微镜

blocks.en_text: through a microscope. And the microbes live so  slowly, for so long that nothing might happen.
blocks.zh_text: 看到它们。而且这些微生物活得那么慢、那么久，可能什么都不会发生。

blocks.en_text: A lot of what we know about them we  got from turning them into a slurry
blocks.zh_text: 我们对它们的很多了解，都是通过把它们打成浆

blocks.en_text: and looking at what their genes could do.  Like “breathing” nitrogen or eating methane.
blocks.zh_text: 再研究它们的基因能做什么得来的。比如“呼吸”氮气或者吃甲烷。

blocks.en_text: We know that the diversity of life in the deep  biosphere must be staggering and that some of
blocks.zh_text: 我们知道深层生物圈里生命的多样性一定惊人，而且一些

blocks.en_text: the most hardcore and extreme beings live down  there. This is a proper frontier of science,
blocks.zh_text: 最硬核、最极端的生物就生活在下面。这是科学真正的边疆，

blocks.en_text: super hard to study and most of  what we know we learned in just
blocks.zh_text: 极难研究，我们所知的大部分都只是在

blocks.en_text: the last 20 years. There is so much  more undiscovered mystery for us,
blocks.zh_text: 过去20年里学到的。还有太多未被发现的奥秘等着我们，

blocks.en_text: that could bring us progress in  medicine, energy, the climate, and more.
blocks.zh_text: 它们可能为我们在医学、能源、气候等方面带来进步。

blocks.en_text: Let’s end by moving our gaze from the inside  to the outside again. Since we now know how
blocks.zh_text: 最后，让我们把目光从内部再移回外部。既然我们现在知道

blocks.en_text: extremely large the deep biosphere is and how  life down there survives without light, oxygen,
blocks.zh_text: 深层生物圈有多么巨大，也知道那里的生命如何在没有光、没有氧气、

blocks.en_text: sane temperatures or not being covered  in poison… could there be deep biospheres
blocks.zh_text: 没有正常温度、还浑身是毒的环境下存活……那会不会有深层生物圈

blocks.en_text: all over the universe? Maybe all you need is a  planet or moon with internal heat or radiation.
blocks.zh_text: 遍布整个宇宙呢？也许你只需要一颗有内部热量或辐射的行星或卫星。

blocks.en_text: And a chemical composition that allows  microbes to build the parts they need.
blocks.zh_text: 再加上一种化学成分，让微生物能构建它们所需的部件。

blocks.en_text: Some scientists suggest that there could  be ten of them in the solar system,
blocks.zh_text: 一些科学家认为，太阳系里可能就有十个这样的地方，

blocks.en_text: hiding beneath a seemingly dead and  frozen surface. So as we learn more
blocks.zh_text: 藏在看似死寂、冰封的表面之下。所以随着我们了解更多

blocks.en_text: and more about the life below our feet, we may  accidentally learn about life in the universe.
blocks.zh_text: 还能了解更多关于我们脚下生命的知识，说不定还会顺便了解到宇宙中的生命。

blocks.en_text: You're lucky. YOU dont need to drill dozens  of kilometers through solid rock to discover
blocks.zh_text: 你很幸运。你不需要钻穿几十公里的坚硬岩石，去发现

blocks.en_text: something mindblowing. You can just order  some inspiration right to your doorstep.
blocks.zh_text: 什么令人惊叹的东西。你只要订购一些灵感，直接送到家门口就行。

blocks.en_text: This is a science project crate from our sponsor  KiwiCo who deliver little adventures in a box.
blocks.zh_text: 这是我们的赞助商 KiwiCo 提供的科学项目盒子，他们把小小的探险装进盒子里送到你手上。

blocks.en_text: Let’s explore: there’s wooden components..  and bolts and wheels... and –transmitters?
blocks.zh_text: 咱们来探索一下：有木质零件……还有螺栓和轮子……还有——发射器？

blocks.en_text: It’s the Delivery Bot Kit, that teaches the basics  of radio control in a playful and intuitive way.
blocks.zh_text: 这是送货机器人套装，用好玩又直观的方式教无线电控制的基础知识。

blocks.en_text: This crate is part of the new KiwiCo Labs learning  club – a subscription that takes you along on a
blocks.zh_text: 这个盒子是全新 KiwiCo Labs 学习俱乐部的一部分——这是一项订阅服务，带你踏上

blocks.en_text: learning journey for young scientists to be.  Consecutive hands-on projects help develop
blocks.zh_text: 一段面向未来小科学家的学习之旅。连续不断的动手项目能帮助培养

blocks.en_text: and strengthen problem-solving skills on things  like science, engineering and robots over time.
blocks.zh_text: 并随着时间不断增强解决问题的能力，涉及科学、工程和机器人等内容。

blocks.en_text: There are also different programs available on  topics like world geography, or art & design,
blocks.zh_text: 还有不同的课程可选，主题包括世界地理、艺术与设计等，

blocks.en_text: all with their own high-quality crates  and exclusive online content to unlock.
blocks.zh_text: 每个都配有高质量的盒子和专属的在线内容等你解锁。

blocks.en_text: We’re not gonna pretend this time that we got it  for our own kids, we just ordered it for fun – but
blocks.zh_text: 这次我们不会假装是给自己孩子买的，我们就是买来玩的——不过

blocks.en_text: we can attest that it makes a great gift for any  niece, nephew, godchild or other little one in
blocks.zh_text: 我们可以保证，它是送给任何侄女、侄子、教子或你生活中其他小朋友的绝佳礼物。

blocks.en_text: your life. We like KiwiCo because with their  new learning club program they are fostering
blocks.zh_text: 我们喜欢 KiwiCo，因为通过他们全新的学习俱乐部项目，他们正在培养

blocks.en_text: a mindset of making learning something that is  an ongoing exploration, just like we want to.
blocks.zh_text: 一种把学习当作持续探索的心态，这正是我们想要的。

blocks.en_text: If you want to try out the new KiwiCo clubs,  click on the link in the infobox or use the
blocks.zh_text: 如果你想试试全新的 KiwiCo 俱乐部，点击信息框里的链接，或者使用

blocks.en_text: code KURZGESAGT to get 50% off your first  month of a monthly subscription to KiwiCo.
blocks.zh_text: 优惠码 KURZGESAGT，订阅 KiwiCo 月度服务首月可享五折优惠。
